name: dispatch-table
axis: function values called indirectly: a 4-way dispatch table, as an if/else chain, as an array of function values, and as a function-valued struct field
notes: The shape every plugin registry, bytecode interpreter and state machine has. Three phases fold the same serial accumulator over the same 4-way rotation, so all three print the same number (equivalence self-check) and values stay under 2^20 so no overflow rules are involved. Rust uses plain `fn(i32) -> i32` pointers (a Box<dyn Fn> would add a vtable the other three do not have). THE FINDING — per-phase at n=50,000,000 (min-of-3, prebuilt module for VL): if/else chain Rust 0.027s / V8 0.063s / VL 0.109s; array of function values Rust 0.056s / V8 0.169s / VL 0.578s; function value in a struct field Rust 0.054s / V8 0.173s / VL 0.591s. Going indirect costs Rust 2.1x, V8 2.7x, and VL 5.3x over its own direct-call floor — about 11.5ns (roughly 55-65 cycles) per indirect call in VL versus 3.4ns in V8 and 1.1ns in Rust. Unlike lambda-hot, `vl build -O3` does NOT help here (1.469s vs 1.331s unoptimized) because the target really is dynamic, so binaryen cannot devirtualise it: this is the raw cost of VL's call_ref sequence (two struct.get loads off the closure record plus a `ref.cast (ref $sig)` on the funcref before the call_ref). Totals at n=50M: rust 0.148s, deno 0.410s, VL 1.331s (9.0x Rust, 3.2x deno), python(5M) 1.202s. Scale-verified 50M->100M: rust 2.08x, deno 1.82x, VL 1.88x, python 2.5M->5M 2.12x. Python's N is 1/10.

audit.startupFloor: Rust column is 144ms (min-of-5/7, taskset -c 2) = 5% process launcher; under the 200ms floor. Subtract the 6.8ms empty-Rust baseline before quoting a Rust:VL multiple. measured empty-program startup on this box (min-of-5, taskset -c 2): rustc-O binary 6.8ms, deno 19.3ms, python3 12.5ms, `vl run <prebuilt.wasm>` 10.6ms.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
